documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
HTN f/u

Doing ok. Work steady. Takes all three meds, uses a weekly pill box now. No chest or back pain, no SOB, no palpitations. Asked about cocaine - says he's 'mostly' stayed away. Didn't want to go further today; I left the offer of a referral open.

Vitals as charted. Heart regular, soft diastolic murmur RSB as before. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
HTN - a bit higher today (ran here from the bus), well controlled at the last several visits. No change; recheck next visit. BMP.
Marfan s/p dissection repair - continue aspirin.
Stimulant use disorder - harm discussed again; referral any time he wants it.
RTC 3 months, video ok.

documents.title: Labs

documents.body: Kidney function and potassium normal again. Keep it up.

Video visit, pt at his apartment, ID verified by name and DOB.

BP check-in. Feels well. No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations or lightheadedness. Taking meds daily. Refills on file at pharmacy. No ED visits since last summer.

Obs: well-appearing on camera, speaking comfortably, no distress.

A/P: HTN on metoprolol succinate 50 and lisinopril 10, no changes. Marfan s/p repair on aspirin. In-person visit late summer with BMP, sooner if needed.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Comparison 08/21/2025. The mediastinum is widened and the aortic knob is prominent. Median sternotomy wires. No pneumothorax. No large pleural effusion.
reports.conclusion: Widened mediastinum with prominent aortic knob.

reports.text: Limited bedside study in the emergency department. Moderate aortic regurgitation. A mobile intimal flap is seen within the aorta. Left ventricular systolic function grossly normal. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Mobile intimal flap within the aorta; moderate aortic regurgitation.

reports.text: Pre-repair: mobile intimal flap in the native aortic root below the prior ascending graft, consistent with Stanford type A dissection. Moderate aortic regurgitation. Left ventricular systolic function normal. Post-repair: valve-sparing root replacement in place, no significant residual aortic regurgitation, normal ventricular function.
reports.conclusion: Recurrent Stanford type A dissection of the native aortic root with moderate aortic regurgitation; after repair, no significant residual regurgitation.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 07/16/2026

CC: chest pain, short of breath

HPI: 30M, Marfan syndrome, emergency ascending/hemiarch repair for type A dissection 11/2024, cocaine-associated alveolar hemorrhage 7/2025, HTN. Sudden severe chest discomfort and difficulty breathing that started about 40 minutes before he arrived. Acknowledges ongoing cocaine use, both injected and snorted.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 daily, lisinopril 10 daily, aspirin 81 daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Exam: T 37.9 C (100.2 F), HR 112, BP 160/55. Distressed. Left radial pulse markedly weaker than the right and the left arm is cool. Inspiratory crackles throughout both lungs. High-pitched decrescendo diastolic murmur, loudest at the left 3rd intercostal space. No chest wall trauma or wounds.

Data: Portable CXR - widened mediastinum, prominent aortic knob. Bedside echo - moderate AR and a mobile intimal flap in the aorta.

MDM: Recurrent aortic dissection in a patient with Marfan syndrome and prior proximal repair. CT angiography not pursued given contrast allergy and findings already sufficient for surgery; cardiac surgery at bedside, to OR for TEE and repair. Febrile with injection use and a regurgitant murmur: two sets of blood cultures drawn before the OR.

Disposition: OR.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIAC SURGERY
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 07/16/2026

Preoperative diagnosis: Recurrent acute aortic dissection; Marfan syndrome; status post ascending and hemiarch replacement with valve resuspension (11/2024).
Postoperative diagnosis: Recurrent acute Stanford type A dissection of the native aortic root; moderate aortic regurgitation.

Procedure: Emergency redo median sternotomy. Valve-sparing aortic root replacement (reimplantation technique) with reimplantation of the coronary ostia and anastomosis to the existing ascending graft. Cardiopulmonary bypass.

Intraoperative TEE: pre-repair mobile intimal flap in the native root below the prior graft, moderate AR; post-repair no significant residual AR, normal LV function.

Findings and course: Careful redo sternal entry. Dense adhesions taken down. The native root was dissected below the previous graft. Root excised with the valve preserved, coronary buttons mobilized, and a root graft sewn in with the valve reimplanted inside it. Coronary buttons reimplanted. Distal anastomosis to the existing ascending graft. Weaned from bypass without difficulty. Hemostasis obtained, chest closed.

Condition: to cardiac surgical ICU, intubated, stable.
Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 07/16/2026   Discharged: 07/25/2026
Service: Cardiac Surgery

Diagnoses: Recurrent acute type A aortic dissection of the native aortic root, status post emergency repair. Aortic regurgitation, corrected. Marfan syndrome. Hypertension. Stimulant use disorder, severe, cocaine.

Procedure: 07/16 emergency redo sternotomy with valve-sparing aortic root replacement (reimplantation).

Course: Presented with acute chest pain and dyspnea; bedside echo showed an intimal flap and moderate AR. Taken directly to the OR; TEE confirmed a type A dissection of the native root below the 2024 graft. Repair as above, post-repair TEE with no significant residual regurgitation. Extubated on POD 1. Blood cultures x2 drawn on arrival: no growth at 5 days. Progressive ambulation, chest tubes out, tolerating diet.

Discharge medications (unchanged):
- Metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Aspirin 81 mg daily

Allergies: Penicillin (rash). Iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Instructions: Sternal precautions, no lifting over 10 lb, no driving until cleared. Cardiac surgery clinic in 2-3 weeks. PCP within 1 week. Cardiology aortic clinic after surgical clearance. Cocaine cessation strongly advised.

documents.title: Phone Call - Mother
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mother called. Declan back at the regional hospital, had another emergency aortic operation last night, in the cardiac ICU. She's with him. Will let us know when he goes home. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you. Front desk please watch for discharge paperwork and book a post-hospital visit within a week of discharge.

documents.title: Transitional Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call. Home since Saturday, mother staying with him. Pain controlled. Incision dry, no fever. Same three meds as before, has them. Knows sternal precautions. Visit Wed 7/29 with PCP.

orders.reason: Stimulant use disorder, severe, cocaine, with injection use; recurrent aortic dissection

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
POST-HOSPITAL VISIT

Reviewed ED record, op note, discharge summary.

S: Admitted 7/16-7/25. Sudden chest pain and dyspnea; recurrent type A dissection, this time in the native root below the 2024 graft, with moderate AR. Emergency redo sternotomy and valve-sparing root replacement the same night. Post-repair TEE no significant AR. Blood cultures negative. Extubated next day, uneventful otherwise. Home 4 days. Sore but managing. Walking short distances in the apartment building. No fever, no SOB at rest.

He told the ED he's been using cocaine regularly, including injecting. He confirms that with me. He says this was the scare that got through: 'two in two years.' He wants help now.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 daily, lisinopril 10 daily, aspirin 81 daily.
Allergies: PCN (rash), contrast (hives).

O: Vitals as charted, weight down ~3 kg. Fresh sternotomy, well approximated, no erythema or drainage, sternum stable. Heart regular, no murmur heard today. Lungs clear. Radial pulses palpable bilaterally. No edema.

A/P:
1. Recurrent type A dissection s/p valve-sparing root replacement. Problem list updated: dissection repaired, AR corrected. Surgery clinic 8/13. Sternal precautions.
2. HTN. Continue metoprolol and lisinopril. Aspirin continues. CBC/BMP today.
3. Stimulant use disorder, severe, cocaine, now with injection use. New addiction medicine referral placed and he agrees to go - referral coordinator to help him book. Repeat HIV and hep C today given injection use.

RTC ~6 weeks, after surgery clearance.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Declan - your blood count is a little low, which is expected after surgery and should come back up on its own; kidney labs are fine. HIV and hepatitis C tests are negative. The addiction medicine office should be calling you; let me know if you haven't heard by Wednesday.

documents.title: RE: Your labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: thank you. that's a relief. haven't heard yet

documents.title: Referral Coordination
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called addiction medicine re: referral sent 7/29. Received, in intake queue; their intake coordinator will call pt to schedule the first appointment, expected in September. Let pt know by phone, he'll watch for the call.

documents.title: Cardiac Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIAC SURGERY CLINIC
Date of visit: 08/13/2026

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Fischer returned four weeks after emergency redo sternotomy with valve-sparing aortic root replacement on 07/16 for a recurrent type A dissection of the native root.

He is recovering well. Sternotomy healing, sternum stable. Heart sounds regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.

Plan: Continue all three medications. No lifting over 10 lb until we clear him at the next check. Desk work from home is fine. He will be seen in the cardiology aortic clinic for long-term follow-up. We reinforced that cocaine is a direct threat to his aorta.

Cardiac Surgery

documents.title: question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hi - surgeon said desk work is ok. I have a client meeting where I'd need to carry a laptop bag and a box of print samples. is that too much? also still haven't gotten a date from the addiction place, they said september

documents.title: RE: question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Laptop bag is probably under 10 lb, but let someone else carry the box of samples until surgery clears you. If the addiction medicine office hasn't called with a date by the time I see you on 9/10, we'll call them together from the office.
